verses.1: You must know this: in the last days there will come difficult times.
verses.2: For people will be self-loving, greedy for money, arrogant, boastful, blasphemous, disobedient to their parents, ungrateful, unholy,
verses.3: heartless, untrustworthy, slanderers, unrestrained, cruel, haters of good,
verses.4: traitors, reckless, conceited, lovers of pleasure rather than lovers of God,
verses.5: having the form of godliness but denying its power. Avoid these people.
verses.6: For they are the ones who enter homes and enslave women weighed down by sins, led along by various desires,
verses.7: always learning, but never able to arrive at the knowledge of the truth.
verses.8: Just as Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses, so these also oppose the truth, people whose minds are ruined, who are disqualified in their faith.
verses.9: But they will not advance further, for their folly will be revealed to all, just as theirs was.
verses.10: But you have followed my teaching, my way of life, my purpose, my faith, my endurance, my love, my steadfastness,
verses.11: the persecutions and sufferings that happened to me in Antioch, Iconium, and Lystra—what persecutions I endured! And the Lord rescued me from all of them.
verses.12: And indeed, all who want to live godly in Christ Jesus will be persecuted.
verses.13: But wicked people and charlatans will advance further into evil, deceiving and being deceived.
verses.14: But you remain in what you have learned and become convinced of, knowing from whom you learned it,
verses.15: and that from childhood you have known the holy scriptures, which are able to make you wise for salvation through faith in Christ Jesus.
verses.16: Every scripture is God-breathed and useful for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for training in righteousness,
verses.17: so that the servant of God may be fully equipped for every good work.

notes:
Notes
- v. 1: "difficult times" is a translation of "χαλεποί" (chalpoi), which literally means "hard" but is used metaphorically here.
- v. 8: "Jannes and Jambres" is a translation of the names given in the text. These are not biblical figures but may reference a tradition or legend about those who opposed Moses.
- v. 16: "God-breathed" is a translation of "θεόπνευστος" (theopneustos), a technical term used to describe scripture.
raw:
[1] You must know this: in the last days there will come difficult times.
[2] For people will be self-loving, greedy for money, arrogant, boastful, blasphemous, disobedient to their parents, ungrateful, unholy,
[3] heartless, untrustworthy, slanderers, unrestrained, cruel, haters of good,
[4] traitors, reckless, conceited, lovers of pleasure rather than lovers of God,
[5] having the form of godliness but denying its power. Avoid these people.
[6] For they are the ones who enter homes and enslave women weighed down by sins, led along by various desires,
[7] always learning, but never able to arrive at the knowledge of the truth.
[8] Just as Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses, so these also oppose the truth, people whose minds are ruined, who are disqualified in their faith.
[9] But they will not advance further, for their folly will be revealed to all, just as theirs was.
[10] But you have followed my teaching, my way of life, my purpose, my faith, my endurance, my love, my steadfastness,
[11] the persecutions and sufferings that happened to me in Antioch, Iconium, and Lystra—what persecutions I endured! And the Lord rescued me from all of them.
[12] And indeed, all who want to live godly in Christ Jesus will be persecuted.
[13] But wicked people and charlatans will advance further into evil, deceiving and being deceived.
[14] But you remain in what you have learned and become convinced of, knowing from whom you learned it,
[15] and that from childhood you have known the holy scriptures, which are able to make you wise for salvation through faith in Christ Jesus.
[16] Every scripture is God-breathed and useful for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for training in righteousness,
[17] so that the servant of God may be fully equipped for every good work.

Notes
- v. 1: "difficult times" is a translation of "χαλεποί" (chalpoi), which literally means "hard" but is used metaphorically here.
- v. 8: "Jannes and Jambres" is a translation of the names given in the text. These are not biblical figures but may reference a tradition or legend about those who opposed Moses.
- v. 16: "God-breathed" is a translation of "θεόπνευστος" (theopneustos), a technical term used to describe scripture.
